description.narrative:
Malnutrition and Livelihoods: Tackle malnutrition enhancing the knowledge and food security of pregnant and lactating women and supporting malnourished children with a quality referral system • Implement Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) approach which is an integrated approach to managing landscapes and ecosystems - cropland, livestock, forests and water sources - that address the interlinked challenges of food security and accelerating household vulnerability to climate change • improve and diversify livelihoods at HH and community level with vegetable growing agriculture through traditional jaden lakou models, collective IGA with Mothers Clubs. This will contribute to the IGA for the most vulnerable women and enhance their economic empowerment
WASH: • Improved watershed management, will not only reduce land erosion and increase rainwater infiltration into the subsoil, but it will also contribute to raising the water table and water quantity at catchment level • Protecting and restoring natural springs, the main resource for agricultural production and water for human consumption. • Improved DRR abilities of the community to face the hurricane season through training and building improved coping mechanisms against water related hazards in a more resilient environment. • Nature-based solutions and climate-smart agriculture will combine throughout the watershed to adapt to new rain patterns and climate change.
Sud- Est - Arrondisement Jacmel. Cayes Jacmel and Marigot

The project will operate on two principal areas of focus: 1. Food Security, nutrition and Resilient Livelihoods and 2. Water, sanitation and hygiene. It will also include targeted activities that enhance a better integration of protection, gender and inclusion in the program. The overall objective is to enhance resilience of communities exposed to food insecurity in Southeast Region, Jacmel district.

At the end of the project, 104 out of 546 individuals surveyed reported experiencing diarrhea in the past seven days, accounting for 19% of the surveyed population. It is not possible to conclude a reduction in incidence because the baseline and endline data are not comparable. The surveys were conducted on different populations and during different periods, meaning that external factors such as seasonal variations or population-specific conditions could have influenced the results. Therefore, any observed differences cannot be directly attributed to the project’s impact.
